summary: /api/risk/close used the SERVER's wall-clock time instead of the broker event's own timestamp, so a close processed even slightly after midnight (or any replayed/delayed event) silently posted to the WRONG trading day's ledger - meaning the daily-loss-limit and consecutive-loss protections could silently fail to trigger on the day they actually should

expected: The day's ledger reflects the loss; the next decision on that day is blocked
actual: Decision on the correct day showed an EMPTY ledger - the close had been recorded under the container's current wall-clock date
root_cause: not the date I told the decision endpoint about

summary: onTradeClosed() computed the daily max-loss threshold as capital*0.05 instead of using the already-injected, dedicated maxDailyLoss field (trading.max.loss) - the configured limit was never actually enforced, and whenever `capital` wasn't populated (e.g. a plain unit test, or any profile that only sets trading.max.loss) the threshold silently became 0, breaching on the very first paisa of loss
repro: Configure trading.max.loss to a value independent of 5% of capital (or leave capital unset) and close a trade with a small loss
expected: Breach fires only once cumulative daily PnL crosses the configured maxDailyLoss
actual: With capital unset/0, ANY negative PnL (even -1) tripped the breach; with capital set, the breach threshold silently tracked 5% of capital and ignored the operator's configured trading.max.loss entirely
root_cause: A literal `capital * 0.05` expression was used in place of the existing `maxDailyLoss` field, which was already wired via @Value("${trading.max.loss:2000}") but never read
fix: Changed onTradeClosed() to compare against the injected maxDailyLoss field directly instead of recomputing capital*0.05
regression_test: src/test/java/com/pietrader/risk/RiskManagerTest.java::onTradeClosed_noBreachWhenWithinLimit (pre-existing test already set maxDailyLoss=2000 independent of capital(unset/0); it would have failed under the old capital*0.05 logic since any negative PnL breaches when capital=0) and ::onTradeClosed_setsBreachWhenMaxLossHit
retest: FIXED - verified via full `mvn clean test` run (216/216 passing) on branch test_dev

severity: P2 (test hygiene - not a production defect)
summary: The shared tickDto() helper unconditionally set DealerInventoryModelDTO.gammaFlip = Double.MAX_VALUE on every tick, intending a disabled/no-flip sentinel. But ExitEngine.isGammaFlip()'s real contract treats ANY non-null positive value as an active flip zone, so every tick in this class was silently read as a gamma flip - which evaluate() checks before any of the compression/positive-gamma/high-IV rules these tests actually target, so GAMMA_FLIP fired first every time, masking the rule under test. The helper also never populated MarketStructureDTO.compression, so isCompression() could never return true for the one test that needs it. Separately, all 7 tests stubbed positionManager.getPosition("NIFTY") with a hand-built TradeState, but ExitEngine never calls positionManager.getPosition() at all - a dead stub left over from an earlier implementation
repro: mvn test -Dtest=ExitEngineMarketConditionTest (on the pre-existing test_dev checkout of the development branch)
expected: compressionQuickProfit/positiveGammaQuickExit/highIvFastExit assert their own named exit reason; negativeGammaHold/lowIvHold assert no exit; slTrumpsAll/targetTrumpsAll assert SL/target still win regardless of regime
actual: compressionQuickProfit, positiveGammaQuickExit and highIvFastExit all got GAMMA_FLIP instead of their intended reason; negativeGammaHold and lowIvHold failed their never()-exit assertion because GAMMA_FLIP fired anyway; slTrumpsAll and targetTrumpsAll threw UnnecessaryStubbingException on the dead getPosition() stub once Mockito's strict-stub check had a passing test to run on
root_cause: gammaFlip sentinel value (Double.MAX_VALUE) was positive and therefore "active" under the real isGammaFlip() contract instead of disabled; MarketStructureDTO/CompressionDTO were never constructed in the helper; getPosition() stub was carried over from a prior, different ExitEngine implementation
fix: Removed the unconditional gammaFlip=MAX_VALUE from the helper (left null/inactive by default, consistent with ExitEngine's own documented contract); wired regime=="SIDEWAYS" to build a real MarketStructureDTO.compression.compressionDetected=true; removed the 7 dead getPosition() stubs and the now-unused buildState() helper
regression_test: All 7 tests in this class now exercise and assert the real COMPRESSION_QUICK_PROFIT/POSITIVE_GAMMA_QUICK_EXIT/HIGH_IV_FAST_EXIT/negative-gamma-hold/low-IV-hold/SL-and-target-priority behaviour of ExitEngine.evaluate()
retest: FIXED - verified via full `mvn clean test` run (216/216 passing) on branch test_dev

severity: P2 (test hygiene / operational hazard - not a pie_trader production defect)
summary: Four manual, network-calling diagnostic scripts (test_nse.py, test_all_indecies_nse.py, test_scraper.py, ingestion/test_nse_poll.py) were named with pytest's test_*.py discovery prefix even though they are not pytest test modules - they have no test framework, no assertions, and run real HTTPS calls to www.nseindia.com at module import time (not inside a guarded test function). ingestion/test_nse_poll.py in particular runs an unbounded `while True:` polling loop with a live network call every 15s at import time. The root pyproject.toml's testpaths=["tests"] setting already protects a plain `pytest` run from repo root, but running pytest from inside analytics/ or analytics/option_intelligence/ - exactly what you would do to exercise the pre-existing analytics module on its own - would have pytest import and execute these at collection time: real external network calls during what the QA master prompt requires be a synthetic, network-isolated test run, and in the ingestion/test_nse_poll.py case an infinite hang
expected: pytest collects and runs only the real unit tests under analytics/tests/
actual: pytest additionally attempts to import analytics/option_intelligence/ingestion/test_nse_poll.py, which runs forever making live calls to nseindia.com every 15s, hanging the test run indefinitely; the other 3 files make real live HTTPS calls to nseindia.com during collection
root_cause: Manual diagnostic/polling scripts were named with the test_ prefix pytest auto-discovers, instead of being guarded by if __name__=="__main__": or named outside that discovery pattern
